title: A Tale by the Wood Stove
summary: A Minas Gerais-style literary tale about family stories, exaggeration, and truth around a wood stove.

paragraphs.pt: Lá em casa, verdade nunca vinha crua; passava antes pelo fogão a lenha, pegava fumaça, engrossava no tacho e só então ia para a mesa. Meu tio Geraldo, homem de pouca pressa e muita sobrancelha, jurava que já tinha visto assombração pedir café na porteira. Ninguém acreditava, mas todo mundo servia mais broa, porque causo bom dispensa cartório.
paragraphs.en: In our house, truth never came raw; it first passed by the wood stove, picked up smoke, thickened in the pan, and only then went to the table. My uncle Geraldo, a man of little hurry and much eyebrow, swore he had once seen a ghost ask for coffee at the gate. No one believed him, but everyone served more corn bread, because a good tale needs no notary office.

paragraphs.pt: Naquela noite, chovia miúdo, chuva de mineiro desconfiado, sem alarde mas sem pausa. A avó mexia doce de leite com uma paciência que parecia reza. Geraldo contou que a tal assombração usava chapéu de feltro e tinha educação fina: “Boa noite, seu moço, será que me arruma um cafezim?” Minha prima engasgou de rir; minha avó fez o sinal da cruz, mais por hábito que por medo.
paragraphs.en: That night, it rained lightly, the rain of a suspicious Mineiro, without fuss but without pause. Grandmother stirred dulce de leche with a patience that seemed like prayer. Geraldo said that the ghost wore a felt hat and had fine manners: 'Good evening, sir, could you get me a little coffee?' My cousin choked with laughter; my grandmother made the sign of the cross, more from habit than fear.

paragraphs.pt: Anos depois, entendi que ninguém queria saber se o fantasma existira. O que importava era a roda: a lenha estalando, o doce quase no ponto, a família fingindo dúvida para que a história respirasse. Em Minas, às vezes a mentira não engana; ela hospeda uma verdade que, se viesse direta, perderia o encanto. E ai de quem confunda exagero com falsidade: tem trem que só chega ao coração dando volta.
paragraphs.en: Years later, I understood that no one wanted to know whether the ghost had existed. What mattered was the circle: the wood crackling, the sweet nearly ready, the family pretending doubt so the story could breathe. In Minas, sometimes a lie does not deceive; it hosts a truth that, if it came directly, would lose its charm. And woe to those who confuse exaggeration with falsehood: some things only reach the heart by taking the long way around.

comprehension.question: How does the narrator describe truth in the family?
options: It passed through storytelling before reaching the table
It was always written in documents
comprehension.answer: It passed through storytelling before reaching the table

comprehension.question: What did Uncle Geraldo claim to see?
What mattered more than proving the ghost existed?
options: The family circle and the living story
comprehension.answer: The family circle and the living story
